summary: On node1, nginx serves HTTPS on port 8443 using a certificate issued by a local self-signed CA. A systemd timer (cert-renew.timer, every 20s) runs renew-cert.sh, which checks the live cert with `openssl x509 -checkend 120` and, when it is within 120s of its 240s validity window, issues a fresh cert via issue-cert.sh (local CA, atomic file swap) and runs `systemctl reload nginx` to pick it up without dropping connections. This was demonstrated live: two automatic renewals (serial 1000→1001, then 1001→1002) occurred on schedule, each well before the prior cert's expiry, while a continuous curl loop (53 requests, one every ~2s) returned HTTP 200 throughout with zero failures, proving the service kept answering requests across the swap. The mandatory node-restart protocol was completed for the single managed node (node1): pre-restart boot_id and health baseline were captured, the node was rebooted via `systemctl reboot` (ack returned before disconnect, confirmed by a subsequent connection-refused poll), the boot_id changed post-restart, and nginx, the renewal timer, the cert files, and the renewal log all recovered — with a further automatic renewal (1001→1002) observed after reboot, confirming the auto-renewal pipeline persists across restarts. Final state: nginx and cert-renew.timer active/enabled, HTTPS on 8443 returning 200.
actions_performed: Installed nginx on node1 via apt
Built a local self-signed CA (/etc/nginx/ca) with openssl req/ca and a policy config enabling precise -enddate control
Wrote /usr/local/sbin/issue-cert.sh to generate a short-lived (240s) leaf cert, atomically install it to /etc/nginx/certs, validate nginx config, and reload nginx
Wrote /usr/local/sbin/renew-cert.sh to renew only when the live cert is within 120s of expiry (openssl x509 -checkend)
Configured /etc/nginx/sites-available/cert-rotation.conf listening on 8443 ssl using the managed cert/key paths, enabled it, reloaded nginx
Created and enabled a systemd timer (cert-renew.timer, 20s interval) + oneshot service to run the renewal check periodically
Issued the initial certificate and verified HTTPS on 8443 via curl against $NODE_IP
Ran a background loop curling https://$NODE_IP:8443 every 2s while waiting for an automatic renewal, capturing per-request HTTP status and served cert serial
Observed automatic renewal (serial 1000->1001) via the timer with zero non-200 responses across the transition
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, nginx/timer active+enabled state, cert details, curl 200, renewal log contents
Rebooted node1 via sudo systemctl reboot backgrounded with a short delay so the ack returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned, confirming boot_id changed
Verified post-restart recovery: nginx and timer active/enabled, cert files and renewal log intact, curl 200 on 8443
Waited for the next timer cycle post-reboot and confirmed a further automatic renewal (1001->1002) occurred before the previous cert's expiry, with the service still answering
Cleaned up the background curl-loop process and re-verified final healthy state

evidence.summary: nginx listens on 8443 (ss output) and curl to https://$NODE_IP:8443 returns HTTP 200 with TLS handshake details

Initial cert issued (serial 1000, notAfter 03:53:18); systemd timer cert-renew.timer enabled/active running every 20s; cert-renew.log shows automatic renewal to serial 1001 at 03:51:25, ~2 minutes before the original cert's expiry

evidence.requirement: Service picks up new certificate while continuing to answer requests (no downtime)
evidence.summary: Background curl loop (53 requests over the renewal window) shows all HTTP 200 responses, with served cert serial transitioning from 1000 to 1001 mid-stream and zero failed requests; nginx error log shows a clean reload ('signal process started') coincident with the renewal, not a restart
Captured boot_id=2b3a8d87-..., nginx active/enabled, cert-renew.timer active/enabled, valid cert serial 1001, curl 200, renewal log contents
systemctl reboot was launched via a backgrounded/delayed nohup wrapper; the exec call returned 'reboot scheduled' immediately, before the node dropped

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proves an actual restart (node1)
evidence.summary: Poll after reboot first hit 'connection refused' (node down), then succeeded with boot_id=02548236-... (different from baseline 2b3a8d87-...) and uptime '0 min'

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services/data and continued cluster/service health (node1)
evidence.summary: After reboot: nginx and cert-renew.timer active/enabled, cert files and renewal log persisted, curl 200 on 8443, and a further automatic renewal (serial 1001->1002) occurred post-reboot proving the renewal pipeline survives restart; final check reconfirms active services and HTTP 200
